# Protocol version

This Complete Study Report (CSR) v1.2 is based on Protocol v2.0, dated 9 June 2023 and approved by NHSRC and Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) v1.0, dated 8 June 2025.

# Protocol summary

*Streptococcus pneumoniae* poses a significant global health threat, leading to substantial morbidity and mortality, especially in the developing world. Despite the introduction of Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines (PCV), with a 13-valent vaccine (PCV-13) being used in Malawi, challenges persist, including high production costs, limited serotype coverage, and concerns about serotype replacement. In response, for accelerated vaccine evaluations and immunological investigations, a Controlled Human Infection Model (CHIM) was established at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine (LSTM) and later transferred to Malawi with the MARVELS programme at Malawi Liverpool Wellcome Research Programme (MLW), demonstrating safety and reproducibility [@collinsFirstHumanChallenge2015b],[@mortonFeasibilityStudyControlled2021a],[@dulaEffect13valentPneumococcal2023]. While PCVs have made strides, the limitations necessitate exploration of alternative solutions. MV130, a sublingual preparation comprising heat-inactivated bacterial strains, with *Streptococcus pneumoniae* 60%, *Staphylococcus epidermidis* 15%, *Staphylococcus aureus* 15%, *Klebsiella pneumoniae* 4%, *Moraxella catarrhalis* 3%, *Haemophilus influenzae* 3% as active ingredients, emerges as a promising option. Clinical trials have shown MV130's efficacy in reducing both viral and bacterial infections, inducing long-lasting immunity, and demonstrating a favourable safety profile. Malawi, despite PCV-13 vaccination efforts, continues to grapple with persistent pneumococcal disease, emphasising the need for innovative approaches like MV130.
Building on the success of the CHIM in Malawi, with a recent controlled human infection trial with PCV-13 demonstrating safety [@dulaEffect13valentPneumococcal2023], laying the groundwork for the evaluation of MV130's efficacy. The robustness of clinical and laboratory procedures, along with positive participant feedback [@kapumbaStakeholderViewsAcceptability2020], supports the feasibility of MV130 trials. The Malawian context is characterised by a persistent burden of pneumococcal disease, as evidenced by surveillance data revealing continued nasal carriage of vaccine-type and non-vaccine-type Streptococcus pneumoniae [@swarthoutHighResidualCarriage2020]. To address these challenges, the study aims to investigate local and systemic innate and cellular responses to MV130 compared to a placebo. Additionally, the research will explore the modulation of the immune response by experimental pneumococcal carriage, shedding light on the potential of MV130 to prevent nasal colonization and subsequent infections.

# Study design

The MARVELS MV130 study is a double-blinded randomised controlled trial of MV130 versus placebo in adult healthy human participants experimentally subsequently exposed to 160,000 CFU/naris of Streptococcus pneumoniae in the nasopharynx. The investigational medicinal product (IMP) will be MV130 (prepared by Immunotek, S.L.) and a placebo containing none of the active ingredients, only the excipients will also be prepared by the IMP manufacturer. Participants (n=106) will be randomised 1:1 to the two study arms (i.e. 53 per arm). We will closely monitor study participants to ensure safety and tolerability of study procedures. We will measure immune protective responses to *Streptococcus pneumoniae* challenge using mucosal (nasal, throat and saliva) and blood samples. This study is based on the foundation of our NHSRC approved feasibility study protocol (19/08/2246) and the PCV-13 and pneumococcal carriage study protocol 16/07/2519 and will utilise standard operating procedures successfully validated in Malawi. We will indicate throughout this protocol where established feasibility [Established, E] study procedures from the feasibility study / PCV-13 protocols are used and where there are new measures [New, N] for this trial.

The study will be carried out in seven stages:

1.	Screening and recruitment: Potential participants will be screened to ensure health and safety as detailed in the methods section [E]. 

2.	Randomization and treatment: Participants will be randomly allocated to administration with MV130 or placebo[N] in randomised blocks (1:1 randomisation MV130 vs. Placebo) participants will receive either MV130 or placebo.  MV130 or placebo are administered as 2 sublingual sprays (0.1ml each) in a single procedure once daily for 42 days.

3.	Pre IMP administration samples: Samples will be taken before MV130 treatment begins to confirm nasal pneumococcal carriage status and measure immune response [E].

4.	Post IMP administration samples  : Samples will be taken to measure immune response to MV130/placebo and confirm natural nasal pneumococcal carriage status [E].

5.	Inoculation: All participants will be inoculated with Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 6B to the inside of each naris. We will inoculate at a dose of   160,000 colony forming units per naris [E].

6.	Detection of pneumococcal carriage: Nasal wash samples will be taken, according to a standardised protocol, at days 2 and 7 post inoculation(23). Classical microbiological culture will determine experimental nasal colonization with pneumococcal serotype 6B at each time point [E].

7.	Immunology response measurements: Blood, mucosal and nasal cell samples will be taken to determine the immunological response to nasal challenge [E].


## Study Endpoints

**Primary endpoint**: 

* Mucosal neutrophil to T cell ratio (NTR) after 14 days of MV130 treatment.

**Secondary endpoints**: 

* Mucosal neutrophil to T cell ratio (NTR) after 35 days of MV130 treatment.
* Experimental pneumococcal serotype 6B carriage density compared between treatments (MV130) and controls (placebo).

## Sample size

As of protocol v2.0, the total sample size for MARVELS MV-130 is n=106 participants, 53 per arm.

**Assumptions and sample size estimation for primary objective**

The primary efficacy analysis will compare log (NTR) between MV130 randomised individuals and controls at day 14 post-MV130 treatment using a standard two-sample t-test. A secondary analysis will be adjusted for individual participant characteristics that could  impact the endpoint and which may be imbalanced between treatment arms. To inform our sample size calculations, we investigated the distribution of NTR and log (NTR) measurements observed in the MARVELS PCV-13 trial, in the CFU160,000 dose group [@dulaEffect13valentPneumococcal2023].

From the MARVELS PCV-13 trial, there are no major distributional differences between study visits and vaccination groups. The overall standard deviation for log(NTR) is estimated as σ =1.2.
The following assumptions have been made with regards to the calculation:

* We assume a standard statistical significance level of 5%.
* We aim for a minimum power of 80%.
* We assume independent data observations.
* We assume that the log(NTR) measurements are not characterised by severe non-normality so that we can assume the sample means to be approximately normally distributed (guaranteed by the Central Limit Theorem unless severe non-normality, such as extreme outliers, is present in the data).
* We assume a standard deviation of σ =1.21 for log(NTR) common to both treatment groups. This is the estimate we observed in the MARVELS PCV-13 trial data.
* Total sample size is limited to 50 in each group assuming a 1:1 randomisation ratio.
* We assume that 6% of sample will not be able to be processed (for a variety of participant and lab technical reasons), meaning that we would recruit 106 participants to have useable data on 100 participants.

Calculations

```{r}
power.t.test(n=50,sd=1.21,sig.level=0.05,power=0.8,alternative="two.sided")
```

With the above assumptions, the study will be able to detect a difference in log(NTR) between both groups of 0.69 with 80% power. This corresponds to a standardised effect size of 0.57 which is typically regarded as a moderate effect size.
With the caveat that the average of a log is not the log of an average (meaning the calculation that follows is not correct and should only be viewed as a very rough guide), this corresponds to a relative change in NTR of 98.32% (i.e. slightly less than a doubling).


**Power graphs**

To visualise the sensitivity of the study power on sample size (assuming the same effect size as above), we produce the graph below based on the above parameters.

```{r}
#| label: fig-powercurve
#| fig-cap: "Power curve based on two-sample t test power calculation."

power_plot <- pwr.t.test(d = 0.57, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80)

plot(power_plot)
```


## Objectives

*Main objective*

To investigate the immunological effect of MV130 in Malawian adult population and its influence on pneumococcal colonisation.

*Secondary objectives*

1.	To examine local and systemic innate, cellular responses to MV130 compared to placebo.
2.	To examine the modulation of the immune effect on MV130 by experimental pneumococcal serotype 6B carriage.
3.	To determine if MV130 treatment is protective against experimental pneumococcal serotype 6B carriage in healthy adults.
4.  To determine the effect of compliance to MV130 on its immunological effects and colonisation by experimental strain 6B.

# Data loading

To be able to do the analysis, we will need to read in the locked, unblinded data. We will then reformat the data to meet analysis needs.

That is what this section does - not visual output, just R code.

```{r readData}
randoDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/MV130_UNBLINIDNG_raw.csv")
screenDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/MV1301_SCREENING_label.csv")
visitDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/MV1302_Visits_raw.csv")
carriageDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/MV130_CARRIAGE_20250610.csv")
adhereDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/vmv130_adherence_raw.csv")
withdrawDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260608/MV1304_Withdraw_raw.csv")

screenDf<-screenDf %>% dplyr::filter(!(pid=="MV11054" & rid_verified==""))
  # PID MV11054 appears twice in data table; they tested positive for Covid-19 on their first visit 2024-10-31, and were rescreened on 2024-11-11 when they were negative and then recruited and randomised at that occasion; so will only use the data from the visit when they were randomised.

screenDf<-screenDf %>%
  dplyr::select(!bmi) %>% # bmi in database seems to be weight*height rather than weight/height^2
  dplyr::mutate(
    bmi=weight/height^2
  )

adhereDf$dayscomplete[adhereDf$pid=="MV10395"]<-41 # hard-coded; needs database update; see email from Vusi from 9 July 2025

withdrawDf<-withdrawDf %>%
  dplyr::filter(pid!="MV10346") # hard-coded fix to a mistaken entry into the withdrawal data frame; MV10346 showed up late but did get inoculated; see email from Lumbani from 29 July 2025

randoDf<-randoDf %>% dplyr::filter(!(pid=="MV11054" & rid_verified==""))
  # as per earlier note: PID MV11054 appears twice in data table; they tested positive for Covid-19 on their first visit 2024-10-31, and were rescreened on 2024-11-11 when they were negative and then recruited and randomised at that occasion; so will only use the data from the visit when they were randomised.

labNtrDf<-read.csv("../Data/20260604_NTR/MV130 Nasal Cellular Response_Revised-AK_GT_LM_04062026.csv")

labNtrDf<-labNtrDf %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Visit=factor(Visit,levels=c("D0","D14","D35","D44","D49")),
    PID_SID=paste(sep="_",PID,sid),
    PID_Visit=paste(sep="_",PID,Visit),
    neutroEpithRatio=Absolute.Neutrophil.Count/Absolute.Epithelial.Cell.Count,
    tcellEpithRatio=Absolute.T.cell.Count/Absolute.Epithelial.Cell.Count
  )

colnames(labNtrDf)[colnames(labNtrDf)=="Neutrophil.proportion.of.all.leukocytes...."]<-"neutroProp"
colnames(labNtrDf)[colnames(labNtrDf)=="T.cell.proportion.of.all.leukocytes...."]<-"tcellProp"

colnames(labNtrDf)[colnames(labNtrDf)=="Absolute.Neutrophil.Count"]<-"neutroAbs"
colnames(labNtrDf)[colnames(labNtrDf)=="Absolute.T.cell.Count"]<-"tcellAbs"

idxFailedQC<-which(labNtrDf$QC.Check=="FAILED")

labNtrDfFailedQC<-labNtrDf[idxFailedQC,]
if(length(idxFailedQC)>0){
  labNtrDf<-labNtrDf[-idxFailedQC,]
}

# removing genuine duplicates (totally identical records)
pidSidDup<-names(which(table(labNtrDf$PID_SID)>1))
tmp<-labNtrDf %>% dplyr::filter(PID_SID %in% pidSidDup)
tmp<-tmp[order(tmp$PID_SID),]

tmp %>%
  knitr::kable(caption="Verifying that records with duplicate PID & SID combination are genuine duplicates.")

idxDupRm<-integer(0)
for(dup in pidSidDup){
  idxTmp<-which(labNtrDf$PID_SID==dup)
  idxDupRm<-c(idxDupRm,idxTmp[2])
}

if(length(idxDupRm)>0){
  labNtrDf<-labNtrDf[-idxDupRm,]
}

# checking for participants with more than one sample for a given visit
pidVisitMult<-names(which(table(labNtrDf$PID_Visit)>1))

tmp<-labNtrDf %>% dplyr::filter(PID_Visit %in% pidVisitMult)
tmp<-tmp[order(tmp$PID_Visit),]

tmp %>%
  knitr::kable(caption="Verifying observations for participant-visit pairs with more than one sample.")

# This duplicated sample involved the screening sample for participant MV11054 -- see earlier notes abou this participant and their two screening visits; resolution: remove sample ID DFU172 as this was from the first visit (2024-10-31) when the participant had tested positive for Covid-19; the second sample DFU17K (2024-11-11) was when the participant was rescreened and Covid-19 negative
labNtrDf<-labNtrDf %>% dplyr::filter(sid!="DFU172")

if(sum(table(labNtrDf$PID_Visit)>1)>0){stop("Warning: duplicated PID_Visit values.")}

labNtrDf<-labNtrDf %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    NTRDiff=abs(NTR-Nuetrophils.event.count/T.cell.event.count),
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    NTRcheck=Nuetrophils.event.count/T.cell.event.count
  )
# NTR is fully reproducible!

labNtrWideDf<-labNtrDf[order(decreasing=F,labNtrDf$Visit),] %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,Visit,NTR,neutroAbs,neutroProp,neutroEpithRatio,tcellAbs,tcellProp,tcellEpithRatio) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols=PID,names_from=Visit,values_from=c(NTR, starts_with("neutro"), starts_with("tcell")))

# consortDf<-read_xlsx("../Data/20250618/MV130_CONSORT.xlsx")
# consortDf<-consortDf %>% dplyr::filter(grepl(pattern="MV",PIDs))
# consortPIDs<-consortDf$PIDs[consortDf$`Grand Total`==7 & is.na(consortDf$withdrawn)]

uniquePIDs<-sort(unique(c(randoDf$pid,screenDf$pid,visitDf$pid,carriageDf$IdNumber,adhereDf$pid,withdrawDf$pid)))

mv130df<-data.frame(
  pid=uniquePIDs
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(y=screenDf %>% dplyr::select(pid,rid_verified,gender,age,bmi,smoking,chichewa,english,fridge,hiv,pneumovac,under5,over65,chronicillness,hivnoart,advancedhiv,pallergy,acuteill,respdisease,cardiacdisease,liverdisease,renaldisease,cancer,chealthcond,medications,pregnancy,pregnancyplan,clinstudy,alcohol,smoking,w_consent),by="pid") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(y=randoDf %>% dplyr::select(pid,treat_name),by="pid") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    studyArm=factor(treat_name,levels=c("Placebo","MV130")),
    sex=gender,
    rid=rid_verified
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(!c(treat_name,gender,rid_verified)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    enrolled=NA,
    withdrawn=ifelse(pid %in% withdrawDf$pid,1,0),
    analysisPopulation=NA,
    complianceSelf=factor(levels=c("Non-compliant","Compliant"),ifelse(adhereDf$dayscomplete>=38,"Compliant","Non-compliant")[match(pid,adhereDf$pid)]), # >=90% compliant with respect to days reported to have taken the treatment (100% corresponds to 42 days)
    complianceBw=factor(levels=c("Non-compliant","Compliant"),ifelse(adhereDf$bottleweight<=30,"Compliant","Non-compliant")[match(pid,adhereDf$pid)]), # >=90% compliant on bottleweight; target weight should be 29g; initial bottle weight was 39g, 10g corresponds to full 84 sprays taken; 90% compliance corresponds to 9g sprayed, so final bottleweight should be 30g or less
    compliance=factor(levels=c("Non-compliant","Compliant"),ifelse(adhereDf$dayscomplete>=38 & adhereDf$bottleweight<=30,"Compliant","Non-compliant")[match(pid,adhereDf$pid)]),
    carriageD0=NA,
    carriageD0_density=NA,
    carriageD14=NA,
    carriageD14_density=NA,
    carriageD21=NA,
    carriageD21_density=NA,
    carriageD44=NA,
    carriageD44_density=NA,
    carriageD44_6B=NA,
    carriageD0_6B_density=NA,
    carriageD49=NA,
    carriageD49_density=NA,
    carriageD49_6B=NA,
    carriageD49_6B_density=NA,
    ntrDay0=NA,
    ntrDay14=NA,
    ntrDay35=NA,
    ntrDay44=NA,
    ntrDay49=NA,
    smokingHistory=case_when(
      smoking==1~"Never smoked",
      smoking==2~"Current regular smoker",
      smoking==3~"Current irregular smoker",
      smoking==4~"Ex-smoker who gave up within past 6 months",
      smoking==5~"Ex-smoker who gave up more than 6 months ago with more than 10 pack-year history",
      smoking==6~"Ex-smoker who gave up more than 6 months ago with less than 10 pack-year history",
      TRUE~NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    enrolled=ifelse(!is.na(rid) & rid!="",1,0),
    inoculated=ifelse(pid %in% c(visitDf$pid[visitDf$visit==4 & visitDf$inoculation_complete==1],"MV10148"),1,0) # hard-coded; requires database update; see email from Lumbani from 28 July 2025
  )

for(i in 1:nrow(mv130df)){
  if(sum(carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i])==1){
    mv130df$carriageD0[i]<-carriageDf$Result[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
    mv130df$carriageD0_density[i]<-carriageDf$density[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
  }
  if(sum(carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B1" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i])==1){
    mv130df$carriageD14[i]<-carriageDf$Result[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B1" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
    mv130df$carriageD14_density[i]<-carriageDf$density[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit B1" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
  }
  if(sum(carriageDf$Visit=="Visit C" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i])==1){
    mv130df$carriageD21[i]<-carriageDf$Result[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit C" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
    mv130df$carriageD21_density[i]<-carriageDf$density[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit C" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
  }
  if(sum(carriageDf$Visit=="Visit E" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i])==1){
    mv130df$carriageD44[i]<-carriageDf$Result[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit E" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
    mv130df$carriageD44_density[i]<-carriageDf$density[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit E" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
  }
  if(sum(carriageDf$Visit=="Visit F" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i])==1){
    mv130df$carriageD49[i]<-carriageDf$Result[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit F" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
    mv130df$carriageD49_density[i]<-carriageDf$density[carriageDf$Visit=="Visit F" & carriageDf$IdNumber==mv130df$pid[i]]
  }
}

    ntrDay49=labNtrWideDf$NTR_D49[match(pid,labNtrWideDf$PID)],

tmpVisits<-visitDf %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pid) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nVisits=n(),.groups="drop")

mv130df<-mv130df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    nVisits=tmpVisits$nVisits[match(pid,tmpVisits$pid)],
    eligibleAge=case_when(
      is.na(age) | age<18 | age>40 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleLanguage=case_when(
      (is.na(chichewa) | chichewa %in% c("","No")) & (is.na(english) | english==0) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleFridge=case_when(
      is.na(fridge) | fridge %in% c("","No") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleContraception=case_when( ## double-check with DMSU,
      (is.na(sex) | sex=="Female") & (is.na(pregnancyplan) | pregnancyplan==1) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligiblePriorPneumoVacc=case_when(
      is.na(pneumovac) | pneumovac %in% c("","Yes") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleHiv=case_when(
      is.na(hiv) | hiv==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleCloseContactUnder5=case_when(
      is.na(under5) | under5==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleCloseContactOver65=case_when(
      is.na(over65) | over65==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleCloseContactChronicIll=case_when(
      is.na(chronicillness) | chronicillness==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleCloseContactHivNoART=case_when(
      is.na(hivnoart) | hivnoart==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleCloseContactAdvancedHiv=case_when(
      is.na(advancedhiv) | advancedhiv==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy=case_when(
      is.na(pallergy) | pallergy %in% c("","Yes") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleAcuteIllness=case_when(
      is.na(acuteill) | acuteill %in% c("","Yes") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleChronicIllness=case_when(
      is.na(respdisease) | respdisease==1 | is.na(cardiacdisease) | cardiacdisease==1 | is.na(liverdisease) | liverdisease==1 | is.na(renaldisease) | renaldisease==1 | is.na(cancer) | cancer==1 | is.na(chealthcond) | chealthcond==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleMedications=case_when( # need to double-check with DMSU
      is.na(medications) & pid=="MV10072"~TRUE, ## hard-coded; needs database update; see email from Lumbani from 28 July 2025
      is.na(medications) | medications==1 ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligiblePregnancy=case_when(
      (is.na(sex) | sex=="Female") & (is.na(pregnancy) | pregnancy==1) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleOtherTrial=case_when(
      !is.na(clinstudy) & clinstudy=="No" ~ TRUE,
      TRUE~FALSE
    ),
    eligibleDrugAlcohol=case_when( # drug history seems to be missing??
      pid=="MV10072" ~ TRUE, # hard-coded; see email from Lumbani from 8 June 2026; should be corrected on database but is not yet the case
      pid!="MV10072" & (is.na(alcohol) | alcohol %in% 3:5) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleSmoking=case_when(
      is.na(smoking) | smoking %in% c(2,4,5,6) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE~TRUE
    ),
    eligibleConsent=case_when(
      !is.na(w_consent) & w_consent=="Yes"~TRUE,
      TRUE~FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    eligible=case_when(
      eligibleAge & eligibleLanguage & eligibleFridge & eligibleContraception & eligiblePriorPneumoVacc & eligibleHiv & eligibleCloseContactUnder5 & eligibleCloseContactOver65 & eligibleCloseContactChronicIll & eligibleCloseContactHivNoART & eligibleCloseContactHivNoART & eligibleCloseContactAdvancedHiv & eligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy & eligibleAcuteIllness & eligibleChronicIllness & eligibleMedications & eligiblePregnancy & eligibleOtherTrial & eligibleDrugAlcohol & eligibleSmoking & eligibleConsent~TRUE,
      TRUE~FALSE
    ),
    completedFollowUp=ifelse((pid %in% screenDf$pid & nVisits==6) | pid=="MV11054",TRUE,FALSE) # hard-coded MV11054 as having completed all visits; see email from Lumbani from 29 July 2025; their visit 2 was recorded on the screening form as they needed re-screening but they did their visit 2; see also earlier notes for this participant
  )

rm(tmpVisits)

withdrawDf<-withdrawDf %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    reason=case_when(
      term_reas==1~"Withdrawal of consent",
      term_reas==2~"Developed COVID-19",
      term_reas==3~"Unwell and excluded by study clinician",
      term_reas==4~"Relocated",
      term_reas==5~"Lost to follow up",
      term_reas==6~"Died",
      term_reas==7~"Other",
      TRUE~NA_character_
    )
  )

mv130df<-mv130df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    reasonForWithdrawal=withdrawDf$reason[match(pid,withdrawDf$pid)],
    perProtocol=ifelse(withdrawn==0 & eligible & enrolled==1 & inoculated==1 & completedFollowUp==1,1,0)
  )

mv130df_pp<-mv130df %>%
  dplyr::filter(perProtocol==1)

# Data Analysis

The R code to generate the results is embedded in this document. By default it is hidden, but can be displayed by clicking on the `Code` boxes on the right hand side.

The reporting of this study is prepared in accordance with the CONSORT 2025 guidelines [@CONSORT2025].

## Analysis population

The analysis population includes all eligible, enrolled & randomised participants who completed all study visits. These participants were analysed according to the study arm they were randomised to.

## CONSORT diagram and participant characteristics.

```{r}
nScreened<-nrow(screenDf)

nEligible<-sum(mv130df$eligible)
ineligible<-character(0)
ineligibleAge<-mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleAge]; ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleAge)
ineligibleLanguage<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleLanguage],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleLanguage)
ineligibleRefrigerator<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleFridge],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleRefrigerator)
ineligibleContraception<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleContraception],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleContraception)
ineligiblePriorPneumoVacc<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligiblePriorPneumoVacc],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligiblePriorPneumoVacc)
ineligibleHiv<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleHiv],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleHiv)
ineligibleCloseContact<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleCloseContactUnder5 | !mv130df$eligibleCloseContactOver65 | !mv130df$eligibleCloseContactChronicIll | !mv130df$eligibleCloseContactHivNoART | !mv130df$eligibleCloseContactAdvancedHiv],ineligible)
ineligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy)
ineligibleAcuteIllness<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleAcuteIllness],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleAcuteIllness)
ineligibleChronicIllness<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleChronicIllness],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleChronicIllness)
ineligibleMedications<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleMedications],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleMedications)
ineligiblePregnancy<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligiblePregnancy],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligiblePregnancy)
ineligibleOtherTrial<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleOtherTrial],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleOtherTrial)
ineligibleDrugAlcohol<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleDrugAlcohol],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleDrugAlcohol)
ineligibleSmoking<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleSmoking],ineligible); ineligible<-c(ineligible,ineligibleSmoking)

noConsent<-setdiff(mv130df$pid[!mv130df$eligibleConsent],ineligible)

nRandomised<-sum(mv130df$enrolled)
```

Numbers for the CONSORT diagram:

  * Screened: `r nScreened`
  * Eligible: `r nEligible`
    + Not eligible - <18 or >40: `r length(ineligibleAge)`
    + Not eligible - not speaking/reading Chichewa or English: `r length(ineligibleLanguage)`
    + Not eligible - not having access to a refrigerator: `r length(ineligibleRefrigerator)`
    + Not eligible - female and not willing to take contraception during study: `r length(ineligibleContraception)`
    + Not eligible - prior pneumococcal vaccination/immunotherapy or previous participant in a pneumococcal CHIM: `r length(ineligiblePriorPneumoVacc)`
    + Not eligible - PLHIV: `r length(ineligibleHiv)`
    + Not eligible - close contact with at-risk individuals: `r length(ineligibleCloseContact)`
    + Not eligible - allergy to penicillin/amoxicillin: `r length(ineligiblePeniAmoxillinAllergy)`
    + Not eligible - acute illness: `r length(ineligibleAcuteIllness)`
    + Not eligible - chronic illness: `r length(ineligibleChronicIllness)`
    + Not eligible - on immunosuppresive medication: `r length(ineligibleMedications)`
    + Not eligible - pregnancy: `r length(ineligiblePregnancy)`
    + Not eligible - enrolled in another clinical trial: `r length(ineligibleOtherTrial)`
    + Not eligible - history of drug or alcohol abuse: `r length(ineligibleDrugAlcohol)`
    + Not eligible - history of smoking: `r length(ineligibleSmoking)`
    + Did not consent: `r length(noConsent)`
    
  * Randomised: `r nRandomised`
    + Randomised to MV130: `r sum(mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$enrolled==1]=="MV130")`
    + Randomised to Placebo: `r sum(mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$enrolled==1]=="Placebo")`
    
  * Lost to follow-up / withdrawn between randomisation and inoculation: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0)`
    + MV130 arm: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130")`
      + Developed COVID-19: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Developed COVID-19")`
      + Relocated: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Relocated")`
      + Lost-to-follow-up: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Lost to follow up")`
      + Other: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Other")`
    + Placebo arm: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo")`
      + Developed COVID-19: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Developed COVID-19")`
      + Relocated: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Relocated")`
      + Lost-to-follow-up: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Lost to follow up")`
      + Other: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==0 & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Other")`
    
  * Inoculated: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1)`
    + MV130 arm: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$studyArm=="MV130")`
    + Placebo arm: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$studyArm=="Placebo")`
    
  * Completed all study visits: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE)`
    + MV130 arm: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE & mv130df$studyArm=="MV130")`
        + Developed COVID-19: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Developed COVID-19")`
        + Relocated: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Relocated")`
        + Lost-to-follow-up: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Lost to follow up")`
        + Other: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="MV130" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Other")`
    + Placebo arm: `r sum(mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE & mv130df$studyArm=="Placebo")`
        + Developed COVID-19: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Developed COVID-19")`
        + Relocated: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Relocated")`
        + Lost-to-follow-up: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Lost to follow up")`
        + Other: `r sum(mv130df$inoculated[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]==1 & !mv130df$completedFollowUp[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid] & mv130df$studyArm[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Placebo" & mv130df$reasonForWithdrawal[mv130df$pid %in% withdrawDf$pid]=="Other")`
  
  * Included in analysis: `r sum(mv130df$eligible & mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE)`
    + MV130 arm: `r sum(mv130df$eligible & mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE & mv130df$studyArm=="MV130")`
    + Placebo arm: `r sum(mv130df$eligible & mv130df$enrolled==1 & mv130df$inoculated==1 & mv130df$completedFollowUp==TRUE & mv130df$studyArm=="Placebo")`

## Participant characteristics

We present the baseline characteristics of study participants at screening, including demographics, physiological measures, and lifestyle factors. These characteristics provide an overview of the study population. @tbl-participantCharacteristics.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-participantCharacteristics
#| tbl-cap: "Participants characteristics"

mv130df_pp$studyArm <- factor(mv130df_pp$studyArm, levels = c("MV130","Placebo"))

sumFun <- function(.data) {
  .data %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = n(),
      sexMale = sum(na.rm = TRUE, sex == "Male"),
      sexMaleProp = sum(na.rm = TRUE, sex == "Male") / sum(!is.na(sex)),
      ageMedian = median(na.rm = TRUE, age),
      age25th = quantile(na.rm = TRUE, age, probs = 0.25),
      age75th = quantile(na.rm = TRUE, age, probs = 0.75),
      BMIMedian = median(na.rm = TRUE, bmi),
      BMI25th = quantile(na.rm = TRUE, bmi, probs = 0.25),
      BMI75th = quantile(na.rm = TRUE, bmi, probs = 0.75),
      smokingNever = sum(na.rm = TRUE, smokingHistory == "Never smoked"),
      smokingNeverProp = sum(na.rm = TRUE, smokingHistory == "Never smoked") / sum(!is.na(smokingHistory)),
      smokingPast = sum(na.rm = TRUE, grepl(smokingHistory,pattern="Ex-smoker")),
      smokingPastProp = sum(na.rm = TRUE, grepl(smokingHistory,pattern="Ex-smoker")) / sum(!is.na(smokingHistory)),
      smokingCurrent = sum(na.rm = TRUE, grepl(smokingHistory,pattern="Current")),
      smokingCurrentProp = sum(na.rm = TRUE, grepl(smokingHistory,pattern="Current")) / sum(!is.na(smokingHistory)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

reformatFun<-function(dat,var,type,rowIdx,roundDigits=NULL){
  # type needs to be one of "medianIQR", "meanSD", "nProp"
  if(type=="medianIQR"){
    if(is.null(roundDigits)){roundDigits=2}
    tmp<-as.numeric(dat[rowIdx,paste(sep="",var,c("Median","25th","75th"))])
    tmp<-c(format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(tmp[1],digits=roundDigits)),paste(sep="","(",format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(tmp[2],digits=roundDigits)),",",format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(tmp[3],digits=roundDigits)),")"))
  }else if(type=="meanSD"){
    if(is.null(roundDigits)){roundDigits=2}
    tmp<-as.numeric(dat[rowIdx,paste(sep="",var,c("Mean","Sd"))])
    tmp<-c(format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(tmp[1],digits=roundDigits)),paste(sep="","(",format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(tmp[2],digits=roundDigits)),")"))
  }else if(type=="nProp"){
    if(is.null(roundDigits)){roundDigits=1}
    tmp<-as.numeric(dat[rowIdx,paste(sep="",var,c("","Prop"))])
    tmp<-c(tmp[1],paste(sep="","(",format(nsmall=roundDigits,round(100*tmp[2],digits=roundDigits)),"%)"))
  }
  
  return(tmp)
}

demoDatAll<-mv130df_pp %>%
 sumFun()

demoDatByVacc<-mv130df_pp %>%
  group_by(studyArm) %>%
  sumFun()

# Reformat the results table
demoDatKable <- data.frame(
  variable = c("Screened participants", "Enrolled participants", "Included in the analysis", "Sex: male", "Age", "BMI", 
               "Smoking status: never smoker", "Smoking status: past smoker", "Smoking status: current smoker"),

  Vstat1 = NA,  # Placeholder for values to be filled
  Vstat2 = NA,  # Placeholder for values to be filled
  Cstat1 = NA,  # Placeholder for values to be filled
  Cstat2 = NA   # Placeholder for values to be filled
)

  c(nrow(mv130df),
    paste(sep="","(",format(nsmall=1,round(100*nrow(mv130df)/nrow(mv130df),digits=1)),"%)"),NA,NA,NA,NA)

                           paste(sep="","(",format(nsmall=1,round(100*sum(mv130df$enrolled==1)/sum(mv130df$enrolled==1),digits=1)),"%)"),

                           sum(rowSums(is.na(mv130df_pp[mv130df_pp$studyArm=="Placebo",c("pid","age")]))==0),

demoDatKable[demoDatKable$variable=="Smoking status: past smoker",-c(1:2)]<-c(reformatFun(dat=demoDatAll,var="smokingPast",type="nProp",rowIdx=1),reformatFun(dat=demoDatByVacc,var="smokingPast",type="nProp",rowIdx=1),reformatFun(dat=demoDatByVacc,var="smokingPast",type="nProp",rowIdx=2))
demoDatKable[demoDatKable$variable=="Smoking status: current smoker",-c(1:2)]<-c(reformatFun(dat=demoDatAll,var="smokingCurrent",type="nProp",rowIdx=1),reformatFun(dat=demoDatByVacc,var="smokingCurrent",type="nProp",rowIdx=1),reformatFun(dat=demoDatByVacc,var="smokingCurrent",type="nProp",rowIdx=2))

demoDatKable %>%

For variables in the demographics, physiology and life style sections, the percentages are out of the total participants included in the analysis for the respective study arms, whereas for the variables in the study characteristics section, the percentages are out of all participants at that study stage.") %>%

## Primary Analysis

### Comparing NTR between study arms at day 14

In the primary analysis we compare NTR at day 14 between study arms. We repeat the analysis for day 0 NTR as a control analysis.

#### Checking for non-normality

As shown on @fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay14, the data are not normally distributed and as a result we will use a Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare NTR at day 14 between study arms. Similarly the NTR data at days 0, see @fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay0, and 35, see @fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay35, are not normally distributed.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay14
#| fig-cap: "Visual inspection for severe non-normality of the NTR data at day 14 by study arm."

normality_test <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyArm) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    normality_p_value = shapiro.test(ntrDay14)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot NTR at Day 14 by intervention arm
ggplot(mv130df_pp, mapping=aes(x = ntrDay14, fill = studyArm)) +
  geom_density(mapping=aes(col=studyArm),position="dodge",alpha=0.2) +
  geom_point(mapping=aes(y=ifelse(studyArm=="MV130",-0.02,-0.04),alpha=0.5,col=studyArm,pch=studyArm)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Neutrophil / T-cell ratio (day 14)",
    y = "Frequency",
    caption = ifelse(sum(normality_test$normality_p_value < 0.05)>0, 
                       paste(sep="","Outliers or substantial non-normality detected:\nShapiro-Wilk p = ",signif(normality_test$normality_p_value[1],digits=3)," for ",normality_test$studyArm[1]," and ",signif(normality_test$normality_p_value[2],digits=3)," for ",normality_test$studyArm[2],".\nWe will use a non-parametric test to compare NTR between study arms."),
                       "No severe outliers or other substantial non-normality are obvious.\nThe use of a t-test for comparing NTR between study arms is appropriate.")
) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f70b4", "Placebo" = "#e57a23"), name="Study arm") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f70b4", "Placebo" = "#e57a23"), name="Study arm") +
  scale_shape_manual(values=16:17,name="Study arm") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans="log") +
  guides(alpha="none")
```

#### Analysis

As shown on @tbl-primAnal-ntrDay14, there is no statistically significant difference in NTR at day 14 between study arms. This is also shown visually on @fig-ntrBoxplot, where NTR measurements on all 3 study days up to day 14 are shown stratified by study arm.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-primAnal-ntrDay14
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of NTR at day 14 between study arms."

mainAnaNTRDay14<-wilcox.test(ntrDay14~studyArm,data=mv130df_pp)

mainAnaNTRDay14table<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyArm) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n=sum(!is.na(ntrDay14)),
    median=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,median(ntrDay14,na.rm=T))),
    Q25=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,quantile(ntrDay14,prob=0.25,na.rm=T))),
    Q75=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,quantile(ntrDay14,prob=0.75,na.rm=T)))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    IQR=paste(sep="","(",Q25,",",Q75,")")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(studyArm,n,median,IQR)

mainAnaNTRDay14table %>%
  knitr::kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names=c("Study arm","n","Median","IQR"),caption=paste(sep="","Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing NTR at day 14 between study arms: p = ",format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,mainAnaNTRDay14$p.value)))) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

This is in line with day 0 NTR, which are also not statistically different between study arms.

In @fig-ntrBoxplot, we display NTR on days 0, 14 and 35 on a figure, stratified by study arm.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ntrBoxplot
#| fig-cap: "NTR at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing NTR between study arms using a Wilcoxon's rank-sum test."

# Reshape data to long format
ntr_long <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid, carriage_6B, studyArm, ntrDay0, ntrDay14, ntrDay35, ntrDay44, ntrDay49) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(ntrDay0, ntrDay14,  ntrDay35, ntrDay44, ntrDay49),
    names_to = "Day",
    values_to = "NTR"
  )

# Convert 'Day' to a factor 
ntr_long$Day <- factor(ntr_long$Day, levels = c("ntrDay0", "ntrDay14", "ntrDay35", "ntrDay44", "ntrDay49"), labels = c("Day 0", "Day 14", "Day 35", "Day 44", "Day 49"))

nMat<-ntr_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Day,studyArm) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n=sum(!is.na(NTR)),.groups="drop")

ggplot(ntr_long, aes(x = Day, y = NTR, fill = studyArm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2))+
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "",
    y = "Neutrophil to T-cell ratio (NTR)",
    fill = "Intervention Arm"
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f77b4", "Placebo" = "#ff7f0e")) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),  
  )+
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", aes(group=studyArm, label = ifelse(..p.. < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", ..p..))), label.x = 1.5, label.y = 2, size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = nMat,mapping = aes(x = Day, y = 0.05, col = studyArm, group = studyArm, label = paste0("n=", n)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f77b4", "Placebo" = "#ff7f0e"),guide="none") +
  theme_bw()
```

### Day 35 NTR comparison

#### Checking for non-normality

As already mentioned, the day 35 NTR data are also not normally distributed (@fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay35).

```{r}
#| label: fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay35
#| fig-cap: "Visual inspection for severe non-normality of the NTR data at day 35 by study arm."

normality_test <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyArm) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    normality_p_value = shapiro.test(ntrDay35)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot NTR at Day 14 by intervention arm
ggplot(mv130df_pp, mapping=aes(x = ntrDay35, fill = studyArm)) +
  geom_density(mapping=aes(col=studyArm),position="dodge",alpha=0.2) +
  geom_point(mapping=aes(y=ifelse(studyArm=="MV130",-0.02,-0.04),alpha=0.5,col=studyArm,pch=studyArm)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Neutrophil / T-cell ratio (day 35)",
    y = "Frequency",
    caption = ifelse(sum(normality_test$normality_p_value < 0.05)>0, 
                       paste(sep="","Outliers or substantial non-normality detected:\nShapiro-Wilk p = ",signif(normality_test$normality_p_value[1],digits=3)," for ",normality_test$studyArm[1]," and ",signif(normality_test$normality_p_value[2],digits=3)," for ",normality_test$studyArm[2],".\nWe will use a non-parametric test to compare NTR between study arms."),
                       "No severe outliers or other substantial non-normality are obvious.\nThe use of a t-test for comparing NTR between study arms is appropriate.")
) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f70b4", "Placebo" = "#e57a23"), name="Study arm") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("MV130" = "#1f70b4", "Placebo" = "#e57a23"), name="Study arm") +
  scale_shape_manual(values=16:17,name="Study arm") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans="log") +
  guides(alpha="none")
```

#### Analysis

The NTR distributions are not statistically different between study arms.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-primAnal-ntrDay35
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of NTR at day 35 between study arms."

mainAnaNTRDay35<-wilcox.test(ntrDay35~studyArm,data=mv130df_pp)

mainAnaNTRDay35table<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyArm) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n=sum(!is.na(ntrDay35)),
    median=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,median(ntrDay35,na.rm=T))),
    Q25=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,quantile(ntrDay35,prob=0.25,na.rm=T))),
    Q75=format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,quantile(ntrDay35,prob=0.75,na.rm=T)))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    IQR=paste(sep="","(",Q25,",",Q75,")")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(studyArm,n,median,IQR)

mainAnaNTRDay35table %>%
  knitr::kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names=c("Study arm","n","Median","IQR"),caption=paste(sep="","Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing NTR at day 35 between study arms: p = ",format(nsmall=3,round(digits=3,mainAnaNTRDay35$p.value)))) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

### NTR response by carriage status

We compare NTR at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 between carriage groups. NTR at days 0 and 14 is probably not very meaningful however, given these time points were before carriage assessment.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ntrByCarriage
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 NTR between experimental carriage groups."

# Reshape data to long format
ntr_long <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid, carriage_6B, studyArm, ntrDay0, ntrDay14, ntrDay35, ntrDay44, ntrDay49) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(ntrDay0, ntrDay14, ntrDay35, ntrDay44, ntrDay49),
    names_to = "Day",
    values_to = "NTR"
  )

# Convert 'Day' to a factor 
ntr_long$Day <- factor(ntr_long$Day, levels = c("ntrDay0", "ntrDay14", "ntrDay35", "ntrDay44", "ntrDay49"), labels = c("Day 0", "Day 14", "Day 35", "Day 44", "Day 49"))


ggplot(ntr_long, aes(x = Day, y = NTR, fill = carriage_6B)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2))+
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "",
    y = "Neutrophil to T-cell ratio (NTR)",
    color = "6B carriage"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("yes" = "khaki", "no" = "salmon"), name="Carriage 6B") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),  
  )+
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", aes(group=carriage_6B, label = ifelse(..p.. < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", ..p..))), label.x = 1.5, label.y = 3.0, size = 3)
```

#### Cell proportions, absolute levels, and ratios to epithelial cells  by carriage status

As requested by a reviewer we repeat the previous graph for other metrics: cell proportions on @fig-neutroPropByCarriage and @fig-tcellPropByCarriage, cell absolute levels on @fig-neutroAbsByCarriage and @fig-tcellAbsByCarriage and ratios to epithelial cells on @fig-neutroEpithRatioByCarriage and @fig-tcellEpithRatioByCarriage.

### Adjusted analysis of NTR data using a multiple linear regression model

#### Model Specification

- Outcome Variable:
NTR at Day 14 (log-transformed given non-normality of the NTR data).

- Independent Variables:
Treatment group (MV130 vs. Placebo).
Baseline characteristics: Age, sex, prior infections (baseline carriage for NC and NVT), and baseline NTR.

#### Results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-linear_model
#| tbl-cap: "Multiple linear regression model for log(day 14 NTR) adjusted for participant characteristics."

mv130df_pp <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    priorCarriage = case_when(carriageD0_NC==1 ~ 1, TRUE~0),
    ageCentered=age-20
  )

# multiple linear regression model
adjusted_model <- glm(log(ntrDay14) ~ studyArm + ageCentered + sex + log(ntrDay0) + priorCarriage, data = mv130df_pp)

# Create a tidy summary with confidence intervals
model_summary <- tidy(adjusted_model, conf.int = TRUE)

model_summary$estimate <- round(model_summary$estimate, digits = 3)
model_summary$std.error <- round(model_summary$std.error, digits = 3)
model_summary$statistic <- round(model_summary$statistic, digits = 3)
model_summary$p.value <- round(model_summary$p.value, digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.low <- round(model_summary$conf.low, digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.high <- round(model_summary$conf.high, digits = 3)

caption <- paste0(
  "Summary of the adjusted linear regression model fit. ",
  "The results show ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] < 0.05, "a", "no"), 
  " statistically significant effect of study arm on NTR at Day 14 (β = ", 
  format(round(model_summary$estimate[2], 2), nsmall = 2), 
  ", 95% CI (", 
  paste0(format(round(model_summary$conf.low[2], 2), nsmall = 2), ", ", 
         format(round(model_summary$conf.high[2], 2), nsmall = 2)), 
  "), p ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] >= 0.001, 
      paste0("= ", format(round(model_summary$p.value[2], 3), nsmall = 3)), 
      "< 0.001"), ")."
)

# Formatted table
model_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(term,estimate,conf.low,conf.high,p.value) %>%
  kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names = c("Variable", "Estimate", "CI Lower", "CI Upper", "p-value"),caption = caption) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE)
```

#### Model diagnostics

The R^2^ value for the adjusted model is `r round(digits=2,100*(1 - (adjusted_model$deviance/adjusted_model$null.deviance)))`%. This means that while the model accounts for a fair amount of variation, there is a lot of unexplained variation left.

##### Residuals vs fitted

```{r}
#| label: fig-linear_model_residplot
#| fig-cap: "Fitted vs. residuals plot for the adjusted linear model for log-transformed NTR at day 14."

dfResPred<-data.frame(
  pid=mv130df_pp$pid[as.integer(names(predict(adjusted_model,na.action=na.pass)))],
  pred=predict(adjusted_model,na.action=na.pass),
  res=residuals(adjusted_model,na.action=na.pass,type="pearson")
)

dfResPred %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=pred,y=res)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE,col="steelblue",lwd=1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,lty=2,col="darkgrey") +
  theme_minimal() +
  xlab("Predicted values") +
  ylab("Pearson residuals")
```

There are two values with somewhat larger predicted values. These are participants `r paste(collapse=", ",dfResPred$pid[which(dfResPred$pred>=sort(decreasing=TRUE,dfResPred$pred)[2])])`.

Otherwise, the residuals do look approximately normally distributed and with constant variance.

##### Influential observations

```{r}
#| label: fig-linear_model_inflPlot
#| fig-cap: "Influence plot for the adjusted linear model for log-transformed NTR at day 14."

inf<-influencePlot(adjusted_model)
```

Looking at observations with high leverage, 5 observations are highlighted: participants `r paste(collapse=", ",mv130df_pp$pid[as.integer(rownames(inf))])`.

```{r}
pids2RemoveForSens<-mv130df_pp$pid[as.integer(rownames(inf))]
```

##### Sensitivity analysis

As a sensitivity analysis we remove the observations flagged as influential observations. These are observations `r paste(collapse=", ",pids2RemoveForSens)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-linear_model_sens
#| tbl-cap: "Summary table for the sensitivity analysis for the multiple linear regression model for log(day 14 NTR) adjusted for participant characteristics after removing potentially influential observations."

adjusted_model_sensitivity <- glm(log(ntrDay14) ~ studyArm + ageCentered + sex + log(ntrDay0) + priorCarriage, data = mv130df_pp %>% dplyr::filter(!(pid %in% pids2RemoveForSens)))

model_summary <- tidy(adjusted_model_sensitivity, conf.int = TRUE)

model_summary$estimate <- round(model_summary$estimate, digits = 3)
model_summary$std.error <- round(model_summary$std.error, digits = 3)
model_summary$statistic <- round(model_summary$statistic, digits = 3)
model_summary$p.value <- round(model_summary$p.value, digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.low <- round(model_summary$conf.low, digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.high <- round(model_summary$conf.high, digits = 3)

caption <- paste0(
  "Summary of the adjusted linear regression model fit. ",
  "The results show ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] < 0.05, "a", "no"), 
  " statistically significant effect of study arm on NTR at Day 14 (β = ", 
  format(round(model_summary$estimate[2], 2), nsmall = 2), 
  ", 95% CI (", 
  paste0(format(round(model_summary$conf.low[2], 2), nsmall = 2), ", ", 
         format(round(model_summary$conf.high[2], 2), nsmall = 2)), 
  "), p ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] >= 0.001, 
      paste0("= ", format(round(model_summary$p.value[2], 3), nsmall = 3)), 
      "< 0.001"), ")."
)

model_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(term,estimate,conf.low,conf.high,p.value) %>%
  kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names = c("Variable", "Estimate", "CI Lower", "CI Upper", "p-value"),caption = caption) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE)
```

We re-fit the model without the potentially influential observations; this model now has an R^2^ of `r round(digits=2,100*(1 - (adjusted_model_sensitivity$deviance/adjusted_model_sensitivity$null.deviance)))`. The conclusion regarding the effect of study arm remains the same: no statistically significant effect.

### Comparison of experimental pneumococcal carriage between study arms

#### Unadjusted analysis

```{r}
#| label: tbl-secAnal-carriage6B
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of experimental 6B carriage between study arms."

pvalue <- function(x, ...) {
    # Construct vectors of data y, and groups (strata) g
    y <- unlist(x)
    g <- factor(rep(1:length(x), times=sapply(x, length)))
    if (is.numeric(y)) {
        # For numeric variables, perform a standard 2-sample t-test
        p <- t.test(y ~ g)$p.value
    } else {
        # For categorical variables, perform a chi-squared test of independence
        p <- fisher.test(table(y, g))$p.value
    }
    #format p-value
  formatted_p <- if (p < 0.001) "<0.001" else sprintf("%.3f", p)
}

tab2x2 <- table(factor(mv130df_pp$studyArm,levels=c("Placebo","MV130")), mv130df_pp$carriage_6B)
rrUnadj<-riskratio(tab2x2)

rrUnadj<-paste0(format(nsmall=2,round(digits=2,rrUnadj$measure["MV130","estimate"])),", 95% CI (",paste(collapse=",",format(nsmall=2,round(digits=2,rrUnadj$measure["MV130",c("lower","upper")]))),")")

carriageTab <- table1(~carriage_6B | studyArm, data=mv130df_pp, overall=F, extra.col=list(`P-value`=pvalue),caption = paste0("The carriage risk ratio for the MV130 arm compared to the placebo arm is estimated to be ",rrUnadj,"."))
carriageTab
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-carriage_visit
#| fig-cap: "Serotype 6B carriage proportions per study arm at post-inoculation visits."

plotDatLine<- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid,studyArm,carriageD44_6B ,carriageD49_6B) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=c(carriageD44_6B ,carriageD49_6B),names_to="visit",values_to="carriage") %>%
  mutate(
    carriers = case_when(
      carriage == 1 ~ 1,
      TRUE~0
    ),
    visit = case_when(
      visit=="carriageD44_6B"~"D44",
      visit=="carriageD49_6B"~"D49"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(studyArm,visit) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n=sum(!is.na(carriers)),
    k=sum(carriers, na.rm = T),
    .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(
    prop=k/n,
    propLow=NA,
    propUpp=NA
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    visitNum=case_when(
      visit=="D44"~2, 
      visit=="D49"~7,
      TRUE~NA_real_
    ))

for(j in 1:nrow(plotDatLine)){
  ci<-binom.test(x=plotDatLine$k[j],n=plotDatLine$n[j])$conf.int
  plotDatLine$propLow[j]<-ci[1]
  plotDatLine$propUpp[j]<-ci[2]
  rm(ci)
}

yMax<-max(plotDatLine$propUpp)
                                 
 plotDatLine %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=visitNum+ifelse(studyArm=="MV130",0.1,-0.1),y=prop,ymin=propLow,ymax=propUpp,col=studyArm)) +
  geom_line(lty=2,lwd=1) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  geom_errorbar(width=0.3,lwd=0.65) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#1f70b4","#e57a23"),name="Study arm") +
  xlab("Study visit (days since inoculation)") +
  ylab("Carriage proportion") +
  xlim(c(0,8)) +
  ylim(c(0,yMax)) +
  guides(fill="none") +
  theme_light() +
  labs(caption="Confidence intervals are exact binomial confidence intervals.\n") 
```

#### Adjusted analysis

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-carriageModel
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the log-binomial regression model for experimental 6B carriage."

mv130df_pp<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(studyArm=factor(studyArm,level=c("Placebo","MV130")))

#Log-binomial regression for carriage status
logbin_model <- logbin(factor(carriage_6B,levels=c("no","yes")) ~ studyArm + ageCentered + sex + priorCarriage, data = mv130df_pp, method="em")

model_summary <- tidy(logbin_model, conf.int = TRUE)

model_summary$estimate <- round(exp(model_summary$estimate), digits = 3)
model_summary$std.error <- round(model_summary$std.error, digits = 3)
model_summary$statistic <- round(model_summary$statistic, digits = 3)
model_summary$p.value <- round(model_summary$p.value, digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.low <- round(exp(model_summary$conf.low), digits = 3)
model_summary$conf.high <- round(exp(model_summary$conf.high), digits = 3)

caption <- paste0(
  "Summary of the adjusted log-binomial regression model fit. ",
  "The results show ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] < 0.05, "a", "no"), 
  " statistically significant effect of study arm on pneumococcal carriage (RR = ", 
  format(round(model_summary$estimate[2], 2), nsmall = 2), 
  ", 95% CI (", 
  paste0(format(round(model_summary$conf.low[2], 2), nsmall = 2), ", ", 
         format(round(model_summary$conf.high[2], 2), nsmall = 2)), 
  "), p ", ifelse(model_summary$p.value[2] >= 0.001, 
      paste0("= ", format(round(model_summary$p.value[2], 3), nsmall = 3)), 
      "< 0.001"), ")."
)

# Formatted table
model_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(term,estimate,conf.low,conf.high,p.value) %>%
  kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names = c("Variable", "Estimate", "CI Lower", "CI Upper", "p-value"),caption = caption) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE)

mv130df_pp<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(studyArm=factor(studyArm,level=c("MV130","Placebo")))

### Carriage density

We can visually summarise the carriage density data per serotype (experimental / natural), study arm and study visit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-carriage_density
#| fig-cap: "Carriage density by experimental / natural serotype, study arm and study visit."

mv130df_long <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(studyArm, 
         carriageD44_6B_density, carriageD49_6B_density,
         carriageD0_NC_density, carriageD14_NC_density, carriageD21_NC_density, carriageD44_NC_density, carriageD49_NC_density) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -studyArm, names_to = "timepoint", values_to = "density") %>%
  mutate(category = case_when(
    grepl("6B", timepoint) ~ "6B",
    grepl("NC", timepoint) ~ "NC",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) %>%
  mutate(time = case_when(
    grepl("D0", timepoint) ~ "PreVaccination",
    grepl("D14", timepoint) ~ "Day14PostVaccination",
    grepl("D21", timepoint) ~ "Day21PostVaccination",
    grepl("D44", timepoint) ~ "Day2PostInoculation",
    grepl("D49", timepoint) ~ "Day7PostInoculation"
  ))

mv130df_long$time <- factor(mv130df_long$time, levels = c("PreVaccination", "Day14PostVaccination", "Day21PostVaccination", "Day2PostInoculation", "Day7PostInoculation"))

# Create a faceted plot
ggplot(mv130df_long, aes(x = time, y = density, fill = studyArm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +  
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +

### Comparison of NTR and carriage between compliant and non-compliant MV130-randomised study participants

#### NTR comparison between compliant and non-compliant MV130 recipients

We can first summarise the compliance data. Participants were considered to be compliant based on self-reporting (number of days they completed the treatment) and bottle-weight at the end of the study:

* Self-compliance is defined to have reported taking the treatment on at least 38 days out of 42 total days (this corresponds to 90% compliance).

* Bottle-weight compliance is defined as having a final bottle-weight of 30g or less (10g corresponds to 84 sprays and initial bottle-weights were 39g; 9g taken corresponds to 90% compliance).

* Overall compliance is defined as being compliance both on self-report and bottle-weight.

`r round(digits=1,100*mean(mv130df_pp$complianceSelf[mv130df_pp$studyArm=="MV130"]=="Compliant"))`% of participants in the MV130 arm are compliant according to self-report, `r round(digits=1,100*mean(mv130df_pp$complianceBw[mv130df_pp$studyArm=="MV130"]=="Compliant"))`% according to bottle-weight and `r round(digits=1,100*mean(mv130df_pp$compliance[mv130df_pp$studyArm=="MV130"]=="Compliant"))`% of MV130 randomised participants are overall compliant (i.e. both by self-report and bottle-weight).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-complianceSummary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the compliance data by study arm."

dfComplianceDataForVusi<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid,studyArm,age,sex,complianceSelf,complianceBw,compliance)

dfCompliance<-rbind(
  table(mv130df_pp$studyArm,mv130df_pp$complianceSelf),
  table(mv130df_pp$studyArm,mv130df_pp$complianceBw),
  table(mv130df_pp$studyArm,mv130df_pp$compliance)
)

dfCompliance<-data.frame(
  Compliance=c(rep("Self-report",2),rep("Bottle-weight",2),rep("Overall",2)),
  StudyArm=rownames(dfCompliance),
  NonCompliant=dfCompliance[,1],
  Compliant=dfCompliance[,2]
)

dfCompliance %>%
  dplyr::select(StudyArm,NonCompliant,Compliant) %>%
  kable(row.names=FALSE,col.names=c(" ","Non-compliant","Compliant")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  pack_rows("Self-reported compliance",1,2) %>%
  pack_rows("Bottle-weight compliance",3,4) %>%
  pack_rows("Overall compliance",5,6)
```

#### Carriage comparison between compliant and non-compliant MV130 recipients

```{r}
#| label: tbl-CarriageProportion_compliance
#| tbl-cap: "Experimental pneumococcal carriage (serotype 6B) at any timepoint by compliance status. P-value estimated using Fisher's exact test."

pvalue <- function(x, ...) {
    # Construct vectors of data y, and groups (strata) g
    y <- unlist(x)
    g <- factor(rep(1:length(x), times=sapply(x, length)))
    if (is.numeric(y)) {
        # For numeric variables, perform a standard 2-sample t-test
        p <- t.test(y ~ g)$p.value
    } else {
        # For categorical variables, perform a chi-squared test of independence
        p <- fisher.test(table(y, g))$p.value
    }
    #format p-value
  formatted_p <- if (p < 0.001) "<0.001" else sprintf("%.3f", p)
}


(carriageTab <- table1(~carriage_6B | compliance, mv130df_pp %>% dplyr::filter(studyArm=="MV130"), overall=F, extra.col=list(`P-value`=pvalue)))

## Post-hoc analyses

### NTR Day 0 vs Day 14, Day 35, Day 44 and Day49 by study arm

We compare, using paired Wilcoxon's signed rank tests, the later visit NTR values to the baseline (Day 0) NTR values, stratified by study arm. This would indicate whether MV130 triggered an NTR response that the placebo did not.

```{r}
days <- mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(starts_with("ntrDay")) %>%
  names() %>%
  sub("ntrDay", "", .) %>%
  as.integer() %>%
  sort()

tmp_summary_long <- mv130df_pp %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols            = all_of(paste0("ntrDay", days)),
    names_to        = "day",
    names_prefix    = "ntrDay",    
    names_transform = list(day = as.integer),
    values_to       = "ntr"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyArm, day) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(ntr, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = paste0(
      "(",
      paste(format(round(quantile(ntr, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE), 2), nsmall = 2),
            collapse = ","),
      ")"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pVersusDay0Ntr=NA)

for(i in 1:nrow(tmp_summary_long)){
  d<-tmp_summary_long$day[i]
  a<-tmp_summary_long$studyArm[i]
  if(d!=0){
    p<-wilcox.test(x=mv130df_pp[mv130df_pp$studyArm==a,paste0("ntrDay",d)]-mv130df_pp$ntrDay0[mv130df_pp$studyArm==a],mu=0)$p.value
    tmp_summary_long$pVersusDay0Ntr[i]<-p
  }
}

arms <- sort(unique(tmp_summary_long$studyArm))

report_wide <- tmp_summary_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Median (IQR)` = paste0(format(round(median, 2), nsmall = 2), " ", iqr),
    `p-value`   = dplyr::case_when(
      day == 0               ~ "ref",
      is.na(pVersusDay0Ntr)  ~ "\u2014",
      pVersusDay0Ntr < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
      TRUE                   ~ format(round(pVersusDay0Ntr, 3), nsmall = 3)
    ),
    Day = factor(paste("Day", day), levels = paste("Day", sort(unique(day))))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(studyArm, day) %>%
  dplyr::select(Day, studyArm, `Median (IQR)`, `p-value`) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = studyArm,
    values_from = c(`Median (IQR)`, `p-value`),
    names_glue  = "{studyArm}__{.value}"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Day)

# reorder so each arm's two columns sit together (median, then p)
col_order <- as.vector(rbind(
  paste0(arms, "__Median (IQR)"),
  paste0(arms, "__p-value")
))
report_wide <- dplyr::select(report_wide, Day, dplyr::all_of(col_order))

# grouped header: 1 col for Day, then a 2-col span per arm
hdr <- c(1, rep(2, length(arms)))
names(hdr) <- c(" ", as.character(arms))

# bold a p-value string when it represents p < 0.05
sig_bold <- function(x) {
  num  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))              # NA for "<0.001", "ref", "—"
  bold <- (!is.na(num) & num < 0.05) | x == "<0.001"  # treat "<0.001" as significant
  kableExtra::cell_spec(x, format = "html", bold = bold)
}

# p-value columns are every 2nd column after "Day": positions 3, 5, 7, ...
p_cols <- names(report_wide)[seq(3, ncol(report_wide), by = 2)]

report_wide_bold <- report_wide %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(p_cols), sig_bold))

kableExtra::kbl(
  report_wide_bold,
  col.names = c("Day", rep(c("Median (IQR)", "p-value"), length(arms))),
  align     = "l",
  caption   = "NTR by study day and arm: median (IQR) and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value comparing NTR measurements from each visit to the baseline (Day 0) NTR measurements.",
  escape = FALSE
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  kableExtra::add_header_above(hdr)
```

The conclusion is that there is a small, marginally statistically significant difference in NTR values at Day 35 compared to baseline within the MV130 arm (with Day 35 on average increased compared to Day 0) that is not identified for the placebo arm.

At day 49, both arms have statistically significantly increased NTR values compared to baseline - but note that this is post-inoculation now.

Please note that we did not apply any multiple testing correction here, but performed 8 tests - so the day 35 p-value, which really is borderline, is fairly weak evidence of a difference.

### NTR trend with time by study arm

The above results are confirmed by using a mixed effect models on log(NTR) values. Minor differences as these model compare means (of log(NTR)) rather than medians (of NTR) than the previous analysis.

```{r}
mv130df_pp_mv130_long<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid,studyArm,starts_with("ntrDay")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(studyArm=="MV130") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("ntrDay"),names_prefix="ntrDay",names_to="day",values_to="ntr") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(day=as.integer(day))

mv130df_pp_placebo_long<-mv130df_pp %>%
  dplyr::select(pid,studyArm,starts_with("ntrDay")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(studyArm=="Placebo") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("ntrDay"),names_prefix="ntrDay",names_to="day",values_to="ntr") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(day=as.integer(day))


modNtrTrend_mv130<-lmerTest::lmer(log(ntr)~factor(day)+(1|pid),data=mv130df_pp_mv130_long)
#summary(modNtrTrend_mv130)

modNtrTrend_placebo<-lmerTest::lmer(log(ntr)~factor(day)+(1|pid),data=mv130df_pp_placebo_long)
#summary(modNtrTrend_placebo)

fmt_p <- function(p) dplyr::case_when(
  is.na(p)  ~ NA_character_,
  p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
  TRUE      ~ format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3)
)

# tidy the fixed effects of one lmerTest model; tag columns with the arm name
tidy_fixed <- function(model, arm) {
  summary(model)$coefficients %>%
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE) %>%                 # keep "Std. Error", "Pr(>|t|)" intact
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Term") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Term = dplyr::if_else(Term == "(Intercept)",
                            "Day 0 (intercept)",
                            paste("Day", sub("factor\\(day\\)", "", Term))),
      Estimate     = round(Estimate, 3),
      `Std. error` = round(`Std. Error`, 3),
      `p-value`    = fmt_p(`Pr(>|t|)`)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0(arm, "__", .x), -Term)
}

mv130_fixed   <- tidy_fixed(modNtrTrend_mv130,   "MV130")
placebo_fixed <- tidy_fixed(modNtrTrend_placebo, "Placebo")

ord <- c("Day 0 (intercept)", "Day 14", "Day 35", "Day 44", "Day 49")
combined <- dplyr::full_join(mv130_fixed, placebo_fixed, by = "Term") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(match(Term, ord))

# grouped header: 1 col for Term, then 3 cols per arm
hdr <- c(1, 3, 3); names(hdr) <- c(" ", "MV130", "Placebo")

# p-value columns: every 3rd column starting at 4 (Term + [Estimate, Std.error, p] per arm)
p_cols <- names(combined)[seq(4, ncol(combined), by = 3)]

combined_bold <- combined %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(p_cols), sig_bold))

kableExtra::kbl(
  combined_bold,
  col.names = c("Term", rep(c("Estimate", "Std. error", "p-value"), 2)),
  align     = "lrrrrrr",
  caption   = "Linear mixed models comparing log(NTR) at each visit to baseline, stratified by study arm. P-values for model coefficients were computed using t-test with the Satterthwaite approximation for the degrees of freedom. Estimates are differences in log(NTR) at each visit vs baseline (Day 0).",
  escape=FALSE
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  kableExtra::add_header_above(hdr)
```

@fig-ntrBoxplot: NTR at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing NTR between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-ntrBoxplotSexStrat: NTR at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm and sex. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing NTR between study arms using a Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-neutroPropBoxplot: Neutrophil cell proportions (out of total leukocytes) at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing proportions between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-tcellPropBoxplot: T-cell proportions (out of total leukocytes) at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing proportions between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-neutroAbsBoxplot: Neutrophil absolute counts at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing levels between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-tcellAbsBoxplot: T-cell absolute counts at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing levels between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-neutroEpithRatioBoxplot: Neutrophil to epithelial cell ratios at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing ratios between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-tcellEpithRatioBoxplot: T-cell to epithelial cell ratios at days 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 by study arm. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing ratios between study arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum test.

@fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay35: Visual inspection for severe non-normality of the NTR data at day 35 by study arm.

@fig-ntrByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 NTR between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-neutroPropByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 neutrophil proportions (out of all leukocytes) between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-tcellPropByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 T-cell proportions (out of all leukocytes) between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-neutroAbsByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 neutrophil absolute levels between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-tcellAbsByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 T-cell absolute levels between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-neutroEpithRatioByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 neutrophil to epithelial cell ratios between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-tcellEpithRatioByCarriage: Comparison of day 0, 14, 35, 44 and 49 neutrophil to epithelial cell ratios between experimental carriage groups.

@fig-linear_model_residplot: Fitted vs. residuals plot for the adjusted linear model for log-transformed NTR at day 14.

@fig-linear_model_inflPlot: Influence plot for the adjusted linear model for log-transformed NTR at day 14.

@fig-carriage_visit: Serotype 6B carriage proportions per study arm at post-inoculation visits.

@fig-carriage_density: Carriage density by experimental / natural serotype, study arm and study visit.

@fig-ntrBoxplotCompliance: NTR days 0, 14 and 35 by compliance status for MV130 randomised participants. P-value at the top of each study visit are comparing NTR between compliance groups using a two-sample t-test.

@fig-ntrNormalityCheckDay14_compliant: Visual inspection for severe non-normality of the NTR data at day 14 for compliant participants by study arm.

@fig-carriage_visit-comp: Serotype 6B carriage proportions per study arm at post-inoculation visits for compliant participants.
